Road · Gran Fondo & gravel

From first ride to the WorldTour

Marine Lenehan · Ireland

WorldTour pro
  1. FebruaryFirst rides: a complete newcomer to cycling
  2. With MatteoA crash course in cycling and personalised, detailed sessions
  3. Within the yearEuropean Gran Fondo & gravel champion (19–34)
  4. WorldsSilver medal at the Gran Fondo World Championships
  5. NowStepped up to the WorldTour: a professional rider

Starting point

A complete newcomer to cycling: she started riding in February.

Goal

Learn the sport and find out how far she could go.

How we coached

  • A crash course in cycling, built from scratch
  • Personalised sessions with attention to every detail
  • Every session different, so training stayed fun and dynamic

Result

European Gran Fondo & gravel champion (19–34) and silver medallist at the Gran Fondo World Championships, within a year of starting cycling. Since then she has made the biggest step of all: she now races in the WorldTour, the top level of professional cycling.

Source: From Marine’s testimonial; WorldTour: Matteo, Nov 2026

“He has not only made me fall in love with cycling, but has believed in me even when I didn’t.”Marine Lenehan
Road racing

From not sprinting out of the saddle to 1,063 W

Tilen Č. · Road racer · Slovenia

1,063 W sprint
Riding time+17%

More hours, no huge weeks

Year before558 h
This year651 h
Best 15-second power+212 W

From seated to standing

Year before851 W
This year1,063 W
Best 2-hour power+20 W

Stronger for longer, set at L’Étape Slovenia

Year before296 W
This year316 W

Starting point

One year ago Tilen couldn’t sprint standing up.

Goal

Race at the front, from local races to the national championships.

How we coached

  • Consistency: steady training, no huge weeks (the biggest was 16 hours)
  • A plan built around his life, adjusted week by week
  • Talking to his coach: RPE and a comment after his rides, so the plan could adapt

Result

4th overall at Portorož and first over the main climb; 9th in the amateur road race at the national championships. All-time bests from the sprint to three hours, and a Critical Power of 375 W.

All-time bests

  • 8 min: 429 W (5.5 W/kg)
  • 20 min: 382 W (4.9 W/kg)
  • 2 min: 556 W (7.1 W/kg), at the Nationals
  • 3 h: 298 W (3.8 W/kg), at Corsa per Haiti

Source: Vekta data, year before vs this year (Nov 2024 – Nov 2026)

“Significant technical progress and gains in strength.”Tilen Č.
Road & gravel

Every number went up

Marco B. · Road & gravel racer · Portugal

+124 W sprint
Best 30-second power+24%

The punch: almost a quarter more

Previous 3 months505 W
Last 3 months628 W
Best 15-second power+124 W

The sprint: faster to the line

Previous 3 months728 W
Last 3 months852 W

Starting point

Marco races on the road and on gravel from Portugal, including the European Gravel Championships in Belgium and Portugal’s gravel nationals.

Goal

Raise his power from the sprint to the hour for his road and gravel races.

Result

From late July to late October, every one of his power bests went up: past 4 W/kg for five minutes, and W′, his energy for attacks, up 28%.

Up across the board

  • 3 minutes: 292 → 325 W
  • 10 minutes: 242 → 263 W
  • 20 minutes: 222 → 236 W
  • 60 minutes: 204 → 211 W
  • W′: 11.4 → 14.6 kJ (+28%)

Source: Vekta data, last 3 months (late July – late October 2026) against the 3 months before

Starting point

Eoin races the IVCA calendar in Ireland.

Goal

Get stronger in the efforts that decide a race.

Result

Between May and November he set all-time bests from 15 seconds to 5 minutes and won his category more than once. In one race, after about 100 km, he still sprinted 1,271 W in the final 10 minutes.

  • VO2max 59, the highest Vekta has on record for him
  • 1,271 W sprint after about 100 km of racing

Road racing

+40 W FTP in under 4 months

Shane Courtney · Tralee Manor West ibike

220 → 260 W FTP
FTP+40 W

Up in under 4 months

Before220 W
With coaching260 W
Sprint+320 W

From about 600 W

Before600 W
With coaching920 W

Starting point

Training 14–16 hours a week over the winter on a generic plan, and getting nowhere. Racing in A4.

Goal

Get faster and move up the racing categories.

How we coached

  • Contact by phone or WhatsApp every couple of days, and weekly feedback
  • No junk miles: every interval has a clear purpose
  • Recovery, nutrition, strength and two flexibility sessions a week

Result

FTP up from 220 W to 260 W in under 4 months, sprint from about 600 W to 920 W. Upgraded to A3 with points to spare, and county hill-climb champion.

Results

  • Upgraded from A4 to A3 with points to spare
  • County hill-climb champion
  • Comfortable in the drops all day, with two flexibility sessions a week

Source: Shane’s own numbers, from his testimonial

“Matteo managed to raise my FTP from 220w to 260w in less than 4 months & my sprint from 600w ish to 920w.”Shane Courtney
Gran Fondo

Qualified for the Gran Fondo Worlds

Bernd Ondruch · Germany

Worlds qualified
  1. 3 yearsTrying to qualify on his own, with no structured plan
  2. Week 1Coaching with Matteo: varied, tailored workouts
  3. 4–6 weeksNoticeable improvements, and consistent since
  4. After a crashThe plan adjusted, never beyond his limits
  5. 12 monthsQualified for the UCI Gran Fondo World Championship

Starting point

Three years of trying to qualify on his own, riding consistently but with no structured plan.

Goal

Qualify for the UCI Gran Fondo World Championship.

How we coached

  • A coaching style adapted to him, with accountability but no pressure
  • Varied workouts targeting different parts of his riding
  • The plan adjusted after a crash, never pushing beyond his limits

Result

Clear improvements after 4–6 weeks, and he qualified for the UCI Gran Fondo World Championship after 12 months of coaching.

Source: From Bernd’s testimonial

“With his expertise, support, and personalized approach, I have achieved my goal of qualifying for the UCI Granfondo World Championship.”Bernd Ondruch
Fitness & weight loss

Close to 16 kg lost in 6 months

Rob Kavanagh · Ireland

−16 kg
  1. BeforeLost interest in the gym and football, and put on weight
  2. New bikeRiding alone, with no progress for the time put in
  3. First callA 40-minute chat, and a structured plan from day one
  4. 6 monthsClose to 16 kg lost: healthier, fitter, happier

Starting point

Had lost interest in the gym and football and put on a lot of weight. Bought a road bike, but wasn’t making progress riding alone.

Goal

Lose weight, get fitter and start racing.

How we coached

  • A structured training plan from the first phone call
  • Sessions planned for him, so he knew exactly what to do

Result

Close to 16 kg lost in 6 months, and healthier, fitter and happier.

Source: From Rob’s testimonial

“To date I’ve lost close to 16 kg thanks to Matteos coaching and support, most importantly I look forward to every session that is planned out for me.”Rob Kavanagh
Sportive & health

From the couch to the Haute Route at 60

Derek Lawler · Kilkenny, Ireland

Haute Route at 60
  1. StartFrom the “couch (literally!)”
  2. 9 monthsA plan built up to the event
  3. 2017Haute Route Pyrenees, for his 60th birthday
  4. 2024Heart disease and a cardiac procedure
  5. AfterA steady, gradual plan back to regular cycling

Starting point

Starting, in his words, from the “couch (literally!)”.

Goal

Ride the Haute Route Pyrenees to mark his 60th birthday.

How we coached

  • A 9-month plan building up to the event
  • Years later, a steady, gradual plan to recover fitness after heart disease and a cardiac procedure

Result

Completed the Haute Route Pyrenees in 2017, “the experience of a lifetime”, and later got back to regular cycling after his cardiac procedure.

Source: From Derek’s testimonial

“As a non-elite or serious cyclist, I can highly recommend Matteo to anyone interested in getting fit and ready for any cycling goal, no matter what level you’re at or what age you are!”Derek Lawler
